description: Held-out, source-linked evaluation pack. Twenty-four customer questions (cases 01-12 from the first revision, 13-24 added in release-readiness revision 02), each bound to one passage in a named local extraction, with a stated expected outcome. Companion review document: docs/HELD_OUT_SOURCE_LINKED_PACK.md, which records this file's SHA-256. Do not edit an expectation after observing an answer; record the answer as a failure or create a separate development case.
missing_source_policy: fail: every extraction named in source_extractions must be present locally with the recorded SHA-256. A missing extraction fails this pack's validation; it is never skipped.
held_out_basis: Every case was selected from source before any model run and was not used to diagnose or fix runtime behaviour. No question, market field or section here is asked by an existing development, canary, probe or deployment case; each case's not_copied_from names the nearest existing material and how this case differs.
review_attestation: On 2026-09-10, KRISH, acting as the independent content owner, reviewed every expectation against the approved own-market source (or the International Sponsoring Directory), approved prospect access to factual FBO eligibility and purchase-policy facts for cases 02, 16 and 24, and ratified the Tunisia, Tanzania, Ghana and Hong Kong interpretation decisions. Claude Code authored the original questions. The external content-review record is HELD_OUT_PACK_CONTENT_REVIEW_LOG_v2.md.

cases.question: I'd like to register as a Preferred Customer with Forever Ghana. Do I need to place an order along with my application?
completeness_conditions: The first order goes in with the application form.
forbidden_claims: Any amount for the Preferred Customer first order: the Ghana record states none.
The 53.000 francs CFA registration minimum, which belongs to the Guinea Bissau and Guinea Conakry text extracted inside the same section.
Presenting the FBO first-order requirement of US$100 as the Preferred Customer requirement.
cases.expected_citation_behaviour: Cite the Forever Ghana directory record.

source.quote: First order required while signing up as Preferred Customer?: Yes, a Preferred customer needs to have a first order with an application form.

cases.source_evidence: Forever Ghana record: 'First order required while signing up as Preferred Customer?: Yes, a Preferred customer needs to have a first order with an application form.' The line sits before the 'Welcome to Forever Guinea Bissau and Guinea Conakry' heading, so it is Ghana's own rule.
cases.provenance: International_Sponsoring_Directory.pdf, record sponsoring-010-ghana, PDF pages 23-26 (line position within the record not established). Quoted on 2026-09-10 from the local extraction named in source, before any model execution. Local extraction match only; not confirmed against the approved PDF.
cases.not_copied_from: No existing case asks about Ghana. The only Preferred Customer first-order cases are UK (evaluation pack) and Algeria (role-scope comparison), both about an amount; this asks whether an order is required at all, in a record that states no amount.

source.quote: (d) Toute différence d’état ou de quantité doit être signalée au service clientèle au plus tard 10 jours après la date de la commande.

The start point is the order date, which the question's wording ('J'ai reçu ma commande') invites the answer to replace with the receipt date.

cases.question: Under Forever Canada's company policy, how many days does an FBO have to report a problem with the quantity of an order?
forbidden_claims: Canada's 10-day reporting rule, served to a GB session from another market's local policy.
A UK rule presented as the answer to a question about Canada.
cases.expected_citation_behaviour: No citation of Canada or US local policy. A safe refusal carries no local-policy citation.

source.quote: (d) Any discrepancy in condition or quantities must be reported to Customer Care no later than 10 days after the date the order was placed.

cases.source_evidence: The only source for the requested figure is Canada company policy 13.01(d): 'Any discrepancy in condition or quantities must be reported to Customer Care no later than 10 days after the date the order was placed.' That policy is country-scoped. The Forever North America directory record, which a GB session may use, contains no reporting deadline, and the UK policy extraction contains no '10 days' wording.
cases.provenance: CA-EN-Company-Policy.pdf, section 13.01(d), PDF page 35 per extraction metadata; checked against sponsoring-098-north-america and UK-EN-Company-Policy.sections.jsonl on 2026-09-10. Access rule from docs/EVALUATION_REVIEW_QUEUE.md 'Already decided': foreign country-specific company policy is restricted; global sponsoring content is not.
cases.not_copied_from: Existing cross-market cases are a US session asking for the Swiss minimum inside German policy and a GB session asking the US opt-in rule. This uses a GB session, Canada policy and a reporting deadline. A US session was deliberately not used, because the US policy's 13.01(d) is worded identically to Canada's.
